skills.name: Gravity and magnetic source modeling
skills.description: Use for gravity or magnetic forward responses from explicit sources in local Cartesian coordinates. Choose point or finite-prism geometry from physical source scale. Confirm ENU axes and signed contrasts. Reject singular/interior observations. Inspect full vector/tensor fields together.

skills.name: Effective rock moduli and mixture bounds
skills.description: Use for mineral mixtures, pores and randomly oriented cracks with known phase properties. Begin with VRH or Hashin-Shtrikman bounds. Select the pore/inclusion theory justified by the physical question. Different constitutive models are alternative assumptions, not repeated measurements.

skills.name: Grain contacts, cement and fracture mechanics
skills.description: Use for dry-frame predictions controlled by contacts, cement, loading, cracks or sand-shale texture. Select the observed mechanism: aligned cracks, unbonded grains, deposited cement, prebonded contacts or shale packing. Johnson stress anisotropy is blocked and unavailable. Supply measured/calibrated parameters.

skills.name: Pore-fluid substitution and seismic dispersion
skills.description: Use for supplied pore fluids and rock frames, including static saturation and dynamic flow. Apply PVT/Brie only within the empirical assumptions. Choose Gassmann for isotropic equilibrium, Brown-Korringa for anisotropic compliance, or Biot/squirt/patch models for their distinct relaxation scales.

skills.name: Layered and anisotropic seismic interpretation
skills.description: Use for fine layering, anisotropic propagation, azimuthal AVO, elastic scattering or impedance. Backus requires subwavelength layers. Verify tensor symmetry before VTI/HTI use. Choose exact isotropic Zoeppritz or weak-HTI Ruger for the stated medium. Elastic impedance requires an explicit reference ratio.
